text: These are the descendants of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, ordained to minister in the priesthood.

versions.text: These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.
versions.explanation: The pronoun "he" has no antecedent in the English sentence (the nearest noun is Aaron himself, who did not ordain his own sons). A passive construction matches the impersonal Hebrew idiom "whose hands were filled" and avoids the ambiguity, while also removing the repetition of "priests ... priests" in an awkward relative clause.

versions.text: These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests who were ordained to serve as priests.
versions.explanation: The stated aim of the earlier revision was to remove the clumsy repetition of "priests ... priests," but the current wording still ends with "priests who were ordained to serve as priests." Rendering the final infinitive לְכַהֵן as "to minister in the priesthood" keeps the sense of the idiom "whose hand was filled" (ordination to priestly office) while reading more smoothly aloud.

text: But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.

versions.text: But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
versions.explanation: Hebrew בָּנִים here specifically means sons; the point is that no male heirs survived to continue the priestly line, which is why Eleazar and Ithamar served. "Children" blurs this legal point.

text: The LORD said to Moses:
Bring forward the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest, to assist him.
They shall carry out duties for him and for the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the tabernacle.
They shall take charge of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and carry out the duties on behalf of the Israelites, doing the work of the tabernacle.

versions.text: They shall take charge of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and fulfill the obligations of the Israelites, doing the work of the tabernacle.
versions.explanation: "The obligations of the Israelites" reads as though the Levites take over debts or moral duties belonging to Israel; the sense of מִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל here is the service performed for/on behalf of the community, matching the phrasing in verse 38.

text: Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are given to him as a gift from among the Israelites.
You shall appoint Aaron and his sons to guard their priesthood. Any outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
The LORD said to Moses:
I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites shall be mine,
for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They are mine. I am the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai:
Register the sons of Levi by their ancestral houses and clans. Count every male a month old and older.
So Moses registered them at the command of the LORD, as he had been ordered.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these are the Gershonite clans.
Their enrollment, counting every male a month old and older, came to 7,500.
The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
The responsibility of the sons of Gershon at the tent of meeting was the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, the curtain at the entrance of the tent of meeting,
the hangings of the courtyard, which enclose the tabernacle and the altar on every side, the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard, and its ropes—together with all the work connected with them.

versions.text: the hangings of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and the altar, and its ropes—together with all the work connected with them.
versions.explanation: As it stands, "surrounding the tabernacle and the altar" modifies the entrance curtain, which is a single screen at one point and cannot surround anything. The Hebrew relative clause describes the courtyard (and its hangings) as enclosing the tabernacle and the altar.

text: To Kohath belonged the clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites; these are the Kohathite clans.
Counting every male a month old and older, they numbered 8,600, charged with the care of the sanctuary.
The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
Their responsibility was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the utensils of the sanctuary used in ministering, the curtain, and all the work connected with them.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he had oversight of those charged with the care of the sanctuary.
To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites; these are the clans of Merari.
Their enrollment, counting every male a month old and older, came to 6,200.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The sons of Merari were appointed to care for the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, and bases, all its equipment, and all the work connected with them,
as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, pegs, and ropes.

Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons were to camp in front of the tabernacle, toward the east, before the tent of meeting, guarding the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
The total number of the Levites registered by Moses and Aaron at the LORD's command, clan by clan, every male a month old and older, was 22,000.
The LORD said to Moses: Register every firstborn male of the Israelites a month old and older, and record their names.
Take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.
So Moses registered every firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
The total number of firstborn males a month old and older, listed by name, came to 22,273.
The LORD said to Moses:
Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be mine. I am the LORD.
As for the redemption of the 273 firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,
collect five shekels for each person, by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

versions.text: collect five shekels for each one, by the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת ("per head") refers to persons, and "each one" is vague after the previous verse; also breaking the final clause into its own statement matches the Hebrew's separate clause ("twenty gerahs to the shekel") and reads more naturally aloud.

text: Give the silver to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those who exceed the number.
So Moses collected the redemption money from those left over beyond the ones the Levites had redeemed.

versions.text: So Moses collected the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
versions.explanation: The phrase "exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites" is heavy for oral reading and slightly ambiguous; a lighter wording keeps the sense (those in excess of the ones covered by the Levites) and flows better when read aloud.

text: From the firstborn of the Israelites he collected 1,365 shekels of silver, by the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the LORD's command, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
